_comment: W16-AW proposals for W16-AY (map + aliases). Byte evidence included. NOTHING here was applied by W16-AW: scripts/target_symbol_map.json, scripts/symbol_aliases.json and config/45410914/splits.txt are other lanes' files this wave.

items.subject: ?Enabled@DirectInstrument@@QBA_NXZ
items.question: AU filed it as 'defined by our obj but no retail address in the DirectInstrument region'.
items.verdict: FOUND at 0x826CCAF0 -- and ALREADY FULLY HANDLED. NO ACTION PROPOSED.

evidence.uniqueness: exact 16-byte relocation-free signature; EXACTLY ONE match in all of retail .text
evidence.why_AU_could_not_see_it: 16-byte leaf touching neither stack nor LR gets no unwind record, so it is not a .pdata BeginAddress and every .pdata-keyed instrument is structurally blind to it (the sub-.pdata stub stratum, CLAUDE.md AUDIT-NC).

already_handled_because: 0x826CCAF0-0x826CCB00 is ALREADY PINNED, into PracticePanel.cpp (splits.txt '.text start:0x826CCAF0 end:0x826CCB00').
It is ALREADY NAMED in target_symbol_map.json as ?InTransition@UIManager@@QAA_NXZ.
That target row ALREADY MATCHES at fuzzy 100.0 (16 B) in unit default/PracticePanel.

?Enabled@DirectInstrument@@QBA_NXZ is ALREADY a recorded folded membership, with T1 evidence, of the symbol_aliases.json group {name: InTransition, address: 0x826ccaf0, survivor: ?InTransition@UIManager@@QAA_NXZ}.
items.why_a_map_row_here_would_be_HARMFUL: The 16 bytes are an ICF survivor shared by UIManager::InTransition, DirectInstrument::Enabled and SampleData::HasData (all compile to the identical relocation-free body). They are one physical copy and are already counted exactly once. Re-homing or renaming the address would attack a row another unit already matches at 100%; CLAUDE.md is explicit that RE-HOMING an already-pinned address is NOT metric-neutral. AU's two-block DirectInstrument carve (ending 0x826CCAF0, resuming 0x826CCB00) was therefore CORRECT and deliberate: it carves around a block PracticePanel already owns.
items.expected_value: 0 bytes. The question is closed, not open.

items.subject: ?SetVolume@DirectInstrument@@QAAXH@Z
items.question: Same AU filing: defined by our obj, no retail address in the DirectInstrument region.
items.verdict: IDENTIFIED at 0x82A478D0 as an ICF fold survivor. RECOMMEND *NOT* NAMING THE ADDRESS -- see risk.
items.action_required: record only (no map row, no alias edit) unless W16-AY also lands the full folded-spelling set

evidence_line_1_byte_signature.caveat: An 8-byte relocation-free signature is NOT identifying on its own. Calibrated against a control: ?IsLoaded@DirectInstrument@@QAA_NXZ (also 8 bytes) matches 58 places in retail. The byte signature alone therefore proves nothing; evidence line 2 is what identifies it.

evidence_line_2_caller_offset.method: Locate the relocation to ?SetVolume@DirectInstrument@@QAAXH@Z inside our compiled GamePanel.obj, take its offset within the owning function, and read retail's instruction at the same offset.
evidence_line_2_caller_offset.note: 0x826970E4 was located independently by scanning retail .text for bl targets before this offset computation was done; the two agree exactly.
evidence_line_2_caller_offset.call_site_shape: lwz r3, -12(r27) (r27 is a biased base; -12 reaches this+0x150 = mDirectInstrument, matching GamePanel.h) ; r4 = the returned int of the preceding _msg->Int(2) call.

items.risk_if_named: 0x82A478D0 is currently ABSENT from target_symbol_map.json. Under the shipped name_check ruler objdiff FORGIVES a placeholder target, so all 17 call sites are presently uncharged. Naming the address converts 17 forgiven sites into checked ones while 15 of the 17 callers are XDK/vendor code serving other classes' setters. Byte upside is ZERO (the one game call site is already forgiven), so this is the MAPID-1 shape: naming an anonymous address pays in bug exposure, not bytes. It should only be done together with an alias group enumerating every folded spelling, which requires adjudicating all 17 callers.
items.expected_value_if_applied_alone: 0 bytes upside, non-zero downside. Recommend recording the identification only.

items.subject: ?GetLocalBandUser@BandUserMgr@@SAPAVLocalBandUser@@PAVLocalUser@@@Z at 0x82682688
items.question: AU-2 recorded that this thunk's callers were never enumerated (W16-AV installed the name).
items.verdict: ENUMERATED: 11 call sites. ZERO contradict the name. The naming is CORROBORATED.
items.action_required: none -- report only; no finding against W16-AV's installed name
items.signature_expected: static (SA): one pointer argument in r3, no `this`; pointer result used as LocalBandUser*.

decisive_corroboration.why: This function is DECLARED to return LocalBandUser* and its entire body is a tail call to 0x82682688 (lwz r3,0x38(r3); bl <helper>; bl 0x82682688; epilogue). The RETURN TYPE of the caller matches the proposed return type of the callee exactly -- corroboration from the type, not merely the argument shape.

all_call_sites.result: r3 live across following member load
TAIL CALL -- becomes the caller's LocalBandUser* return value

all_call_sites.arg: r3 = returned pointer of the immediately preceding call
r3 = returned pointer of the immediately preceding call
r3 = returned pointer of the immediately preceding call
all_call_sites.result: mr r4, r3 (passed on as a pointer)

items.recurring_shape: Six sites share one idiom: lwz r11,0x5C(r11); mtctr; bctrl; mr r3,<user>; bl 0x82682688 -- a virtual accessor (vtable slot 0x5C) yielding a LocalUser*, immediately mapped to a LocalBandUser*. Four of those six sit in ProfileSwapped message handlers, which is exactly where a LocalUser -> LocalBandUser lookup belongs.
